A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same FakeSV-based benchmark, renamed from MVFNDB to POVFNDB. Their complete main texts, appendices, equations, tables, and figures support comparison despite some inconsistent reporting.

before.justification: V1 reports original MLLM evaluations, CoT comparisons and instruction-tuning results in Tables 2–4, together with empirical video-feature analyses.

after.justification: V2 retains original benchmark experiments and reports additional CoT reasoning metrics, dataset statistics, and qualitative case analyses.

M1.justification: Both versions contain the same CoT variants and an instruction-tuned baseline scoring 81.14 accuracy and 80.26 Macro-F1. However, v1 names that model Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, while v2 names Qwen2.5-VL-7B-Instruct and specifies LoRA training. The PDFs do not resolve whether the backbone changed or its label was corrected; the expanded procedure descriptions alone do not establish a method change.

E1.justification: Both versions use FakeSV, six news categories, and the same ten perception, understanding, and reasoning tasks. V2's dataset-comparison table does not introduce additional evaluation corpora, and its new cases remain within the existing task coverage.

E2.justification: The eight main MLLM configurations and basic, CAC, OSF, and combined CoT comparisons are retained. V1 already discusses comparison against zero-shot inference in Appendix B.4; v2 explicitly tabulates it. Newly cited detection methods are not added as evaluated competitors.

E3.justification: Reported settings change: v1 specifies 30 CPP position descriptions, whereas v2 Figure 25 lists 20. Reported test-category shares also differ, including event_np changing from 21.9% to 13.0% in v1 Figure 20 versus v2 Figure 6. V2 revises the annotation-generator description and temporal-IoU matching formula. These are documented protocol revisions, without establishing that experiments were rerun or videos resplit.

E4.justification: V2 adds text-perception failure examples, a detailed train-video reasoning case, and two CoT error comparisons (Figures 4–5 and Tables 6, 13–14). It removes v1's text-area, aspect-ratio, saturation, brightness, and emotion analyses (Figures 14–18). Frame-sampling and key-element sensitivity analyses are retained in Appendix E; much of the renamed rationale-validation analysis reuses earlier feature distributions.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or comparable uncertainty estimates for the model evaluations.

E6.justification: Perception/understanding scores remain unchanged, but FDR accuracies are revised, including Qwen2.5-VL-7B from 70.12 to 68.79. Several CoT Macro-F1 entries also change between v1 Table 4 and v2 Table 7. V2 Table 5 adds extensive reasoning-metric results, including tuned-model ENHR/RHR/KHR of 74.58/83.15/51.37; its 81.14/80.26 accuracy/Macro-F1 already appeared in v1. Unresolved setting differences prevent interpreting these revisions as same-setting performance changes.

T1.justification: V2 Appendix G replaces v1 Appendix B.3's underdefined temporal-IoU expression with best-matching predicted intervals and explicit within-video and across-video averaging (Equations 15–17). It also corrects summation/count inconsistencies. Most other expanded equations restate existing metrics; no theorem or proof contribution is introduced.

C1.justification: The process-oriented benchmark claim remains, but v2 makes a state-of-the-art, fine-tuned explainable detector a central abstract and introduction contribution. V1 instead emphasizes empirically motivated task construction, feature combinations, and performance bottlenecks. V2's conclusion also advances the stronger claim that effective VFND requires domain-specific reasoning strategies.

C2.justification: V2 reframes feature-distribution observations as validation of MLLM rationales and adds interpretations about OSF superiority, inadequate evidence weighting, and the need for domain-specific fine-tuning. It removes the emotion-based explanations accompanying deleted analyses. The limitations replace v1's category-balance concern with the need to authenticate external knowledge through multiple sources.

D1.justification: V2 supplies full task and judge prompts, four CoT prompt templates, and a training-configuration table. Newly disclosed details include LoRA, 12 epochs, a 5e-5 learning rate, sequence length 32,768, batching, precision, and frozen components. These substantially improve documentation of previously underspecified experiments; the hardware, compute-budget, and licensing disclosures are largely retained.

R1.justification: V2 substantially refocuses the related-work discussion on fake-news detection and adds an explicit benchmark comparison with CHECKED, FakeSV, TRUE, FakeVV, and FMNV in Table 1. It introduces references including Sniffer, TripleFact, FakeSV-VLM, and IMOL while removing several general multimodal and news-production references. This expands the evidence used to position the benchmark's novelty.

P1.justification: The abstract and introduction are extensively rewritten, terminology changes to POVFNDB/POVFND-CoT, and related-work sections are consolidated. Empirical analysis moves into Appendix D, task definitions and result interpretation move into the main text, and a conclusion plus dedicated documentation appendices are added.

P2.justification: V2 adds benchmark-overview diagrams, dataset-statistics displays, prompt panels, and case-study tables. Main result tables gain redesigned headers and ranking highlights. Existing analysis plots are relocated or redrawn, while several feature-analysis figures and older pipeline displays disappear. These changes substantially alter the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: V2 improves inspectability and reproducibility through explicit task/judge/CoT prompts, training settings, clearer organization, and a better-defined temporal metric. The overall gain is limited by unexplained differences between the identically named CoT configurations in Tables 5 and 7, unresolved backbone labeling, and stronger state-of-the-art claims without additional evaluated external detectors. The documentation gains are clear, but the scientific comparisons remain insufficiently reconciled.
